decisions.why: The glossary row propitiári (open) renders the family *ser propício*, and 24:11 and 64:4 say *sereis propício ao meu pecado / às nossas impiedades*. Two blind readers (Ps 24, Ps 64) heard God favouring the sin, and both listed *propício* as unknown: in Portuguese *propício a X* is 'favourable to X', and with a sin as X it says the opposite of the prayer. In Latin the dative of the sin after *propítius* is the prayer idiom for 'be gracious about, i.e. pardon' (ἱλάσθητι ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις; DRB 'forgive', MS1932 'perdoa'). This verse is also said alone — the Lenten Tract *Dómine, non secúndum* (78:8–9), the Thursday Matins antiphon of this psalm *Ádjuva nos, Deus, salutáris noster: et propítius esto peccátis nostris*, and the Christmas-season versicle (Nat2-0) — so a wrong first hearing here would be repeated more than anywhere else in the family. Ruling: *sede clemente com os nossos pecados*. *Clemência* is mercy shown to a fault: one can be clement only with what is a wrong, so the phrase cannot be heard as approving the sins, and it asks exactly what the Latin asks (mildness in judging them). It is the plainest word of mercy a Brazilian Catholic knows (*ó clemente, ó piedosa* in the Salve Rainha). *Clemens / cleméntia* never occur in the Latin psalter (grep), so it collides with nothing; *perdoar* is kept for *dimíttere* (24:18; the Our Father's *perdoai-nos*), *misericordioso* for *miséricors* (77:38 has both words side by side). Cost: the Latin's word is not kept in Portuguese where its object is a sin; where the object is a person or the land (98:8 *propítius fuísti eis*, 32:65 of the canticle *propítius erit terræ*) *propício* can stay. Proposed to the row for the whole family (24:11, 64:4, 77:38, 102:3).

decisions.why: The Latin follows the Greek ὀπωροφυλάκιον, the watchman's shelter in an orchard (the Hebrew's 'heaps of ruins' is not followed). The image is a city left as flimsy and lonely as a fruit-guard's hut. *Posuérunt* is repeated at the head of 78:2, so both verses keep *puseram*; *como* gives the Latin's *in* its sense of 'into the state of'. MS1932 *uma como cabana de guarda frutas*; DRB 'as a place to keep fruit', which can be heard as a storehouse. v2: the stylist found the infinitive periphrasis flat and the ambiguity reader heard a storage shed; *cabana de vigia do pomar* names the watchman's hut (*vigia* is *custódia*'s watch) and removes the storeroom. The Latinist asked the result construction *reduziram Jerusalém a …*: refused, because *posuérunt* is repeated at the head of 78:2 and *puseram … como* keeps the anaphora; *pôr como* can say a result in Portuguese (as 78:2 *como comida*).

decisions.why: *Morticína* is properly carrion — the carcasses of beasts that died of themselves (L&S; θνησιμαῖα, Lev 11). Said of the servants' bodies it carries contempt: they were left like dead animals. *os cadáveres* (MS1932; DRB 'dead bodies') is the plain word and loses that edge; *as carcaças* keeps it but is heard as the frame of a car or a slaughtered animal.

decisions.why: The Latin has no object. The project's build for *non est qui* + verb without object is to supply none (21:12 *não há quem auxilie*, 49:22, 70:11 *não há quem liberte*). *Sepultar* without object is less usual than *auxiliar*, and MS1932 supplies it (*quem lhes desse sepultura*). v2: the stylist found the colon cut off without the object, and the ambiguity reader heard a second reading, 'no one who was buried'. Supplying an object pronoun is grammar (D2); the object is plain from *sánguinem eórum*. Taken; 21:12 and 70:11 (*auxiliar*, *libertar*) stand, since those verbs are heard well without one.

decisions.why: *Anticipáre nos* (L&S cites this verse: 'to take before one'); προκαταλαβέτωσαν, 'overtake first'. The mercies are to come before us — reach us before we perish. 76:5 *Anticipavérunt vigílias* → *anteciparam* keeps the cognate. *nos antecipem* is understood as 'get ahead of us'; *venham ao nosso encontro* is the sense but a paraphrase. The plural *misericórdiæ* is kept. v2: the stylist called *nos antecipem* a Latinism that means nothing clear, and the ambiguity reader found it odd. In church Latin *anticipáre / præveníre nos* is the mercy that comes first to meet us; *venham ao nosso encontro* says that motion without adding anything, and is the plainer of two faithful wordings (D2). Taken; the Latinist gate (v2) is asked to check it.

decisions.why: The Latin varies *gentes / natiónes* in one verse; the Greek has one word twice (ἔθνη … ἔθνεσιν), so by D15's test the variation is the Latin translator's elegance. *gentes → nações* (glossary); *natiónes* takes the same word. *gentios* for one of them was weighed: it is the glossary's alternative for the Nunc dimittis only, and here it would make one group sound like two. v2: the stylist asked *entre os gentios* for the first, to vary the repetition. Refused for the reason above; *gentios* is his option. His other point (the repeated *entre* primed a misreading of 10b's verb) is met in 10b instead.

decisions.latin: impropérium ipsórum, quod exprobravérunt tibi, Dómine
decisions.why: *Impropérium* shares *afronta* with *oppróbrium* (D15, the oppróbrium row, 68:20), and *exprobráre → afrontar*, so the figure *the reproach with which they reproached you* is kept as 68:10 keeps it (*as afrontas dos que vos afrontam*). *ipsórum* ('their own') is carried by the named subject *eles* in the relative, so that *deles* does not follow *deles* of the first colon. v2: the stylist heard a same-root jingle the Latin does not have and asked *com que vos insultaram*. Refused: the Greek has the figure itself (τὸν ὀνειδισμὸν αὐτῶν ὃν ὠνείδισάν σε), the Latin's two words are one Greek root, the glossary gives both *afronta / afrontar* (D15), and 68:10 keeps the same figure.

choices.78:1: Bare vocative *Deus* (D44). *gentes → nações* (glossary). *templum sanctum tuum → o vosso templo santo* (as the 5:8b formula row). *vieram … à vossa herança*: *veníre in*, not *intráre*; MS1932 the same. The verse is also the Common of Martyrs' reading (Commune/C3).
choices.78:2: *escas volatílibus cæli* → *como comida às aves do céu*; the esca row names *comida* for food given (68:22). The second colon keeps the Latin's ellipsis of *posuérunt*, with *às* matching *às aves*. *carnes* plural kept for men's flesh (the carnes row). *sanctórum* (ὁσίων) → *santos* (glossary). *béstiis → feras* (glossary). The Innocents' responsory (12-28) reads this verse with *mortália*. The ambiguity reader heard *santos* as canonized saints; the glossary's *sanctus → santo* kept (as 30:24, 31:6).
choices.78:3: *eórum → deles* (not *o seu sangue*, which could be heard as their own or God's). *in circúitu → ao redor de* (glossary). *effudérunt → derramaram*, echoed by *que foi derramado* in 78:10b (*effúsus est*), as the Latin echoes it. The Innocents' responsory (12-28) sets this verse.
choices.78:4: Near-twin of 43:14 (*oppróbrium vicínis nostris … his, qui sunt in circúitu nostro*): the shared words are copied (*uma afronta para os nossos vizinhos*, *zombaria … para os que estão ao nosso redor*); the Latin varies *derísum / illúsio* and so does the Portuguese (*riso / escárnio*; D39 names 78:4). *Facti sumus → Tornamo-nos*, as 30:12 *tornei-me uma afronta*.
choices.78:5: The settled formula *Até quando, Senhor, … para sempre?* (D27; 12:1). *irascéris* future → *vos irareis*. The second colon continues the question without repeating *até quando*, as the Latin (and as 73:10). v2: the second colon in the stylist's order (*como fogo se acenderá*), so it no longer opens on a clitic. *zelus → zelo* (the zeláre row keeps the noun; 68:10, 118:139): the ambiguity reader heard 'care' first; *zelo* beside *irareis* and *fogo* is kept as the Latin's word.
choices.78:6: *novérunt* (perfect of knowing, present sense) → *conhecem* (D44). *effúnde → derramai*; *invocáre → invocar*.
choices.78:8: The Lenten Tract (Quadp3-3 and ferias) sets 78:8–9 with *Dómine* before it; the verse reads alone. *iniquitátum nostrárum antiquárum → das nossas iniquidades antigas* (adjective after, as the Latin). *Ne memíneris → Não vos lembreis* (the reminísci row, 24:7).
choices.78:9: *Ádjuva nos → Auxiliai-nos* (the adjuváre row; 43:26). *salutáris noster → nosso Salvador* (64:6, the salutáris row). *propter … propter* both → *por causa de*, keeping the Latin's repetition (*propter nomen tuum → por causa do vosso nome*, 43:26). *líbera → livrai* (liberáre). The first colon is long (it is long in the Latin: two clauses before the asterisk). The Thursday Matins antiphon *Ádjuva nos, * Deus, salutáris noster: et propítius esto peccátis nostris* reads: *Auxiliai-nos, Deus, nosso Salvador: e sede clemente com os nossos pecados*.
choices.78:10: *Ne forte dicant → Para que não digam* (*forte* absorbed, as MS1932). *Ubi est Deus eórum? → Onde está o Deus deles?* (41:4 *Onde está o teu Deus?*). *coram óculis nostris → diante dos nossos olhos*. The verse ends on a comma: its subject opens 78:10b.
choices.78:10b: *últio → vingança* (the vindíctæ row; ἐκδίκησις is the Greek of both). *intróeat in conspéctu tuo → entre na vossa presença*, as 118:170 *Intret postulátio mea in conspéctu tuo → Entre o meu pedido na vossa presença* (a verb of motion: *à vossa vista* does not take one). *gémitus → gemido*.
choices.78:11: *magnitúdo → grandeza*; *bráchium → braço*. The ambiguity reader heard *tomai posse* as 'seize' rather than 'claim as yours'; kept — it is the Latin's *possidére*, and the Greek's 'preserve' is MS1932's reading, not the Latin's.
choices.78:12: *réddere → pagar* (the réddere row; 27:4b *pagai-lhes*). The ambiguity reader did not know *seio* and heard 'in their midst'; kept, as 73:11 (*do meio do vosso seio*).
choices.78:13: *Nos autem → Nós, porém,* (the ego autem row). *oves páscuæ tuæ → as ovelhas da vossa pastagem* (the páscua row; 73:1 the same). *confitébimur tibi → vos daremos graças* (D5; 74:2). *in sǽculum → para sempre* (D23).
choices.78:13b: The formula *De geração em geração* (118:90). *annuntiáre → anunciar* (D41); *laudem tuam → o vosso louvor* (50:17).

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps078.md (Latin, LXX, WLC, DRB, MS1932; no Diurnal text for this psalm). DO's Portuguese not used (D12). Glossary rows looked up with ps078/gl.py; wordings of translated psalms with ps078/conc.py (both copied from ps070). Liturgical uses found by grep in content/do: the Lenten Tract (78:8–9), the Thursday Matins antiphon (78:9), the Christmas-season versicle Nat2-0 (78:9b), the Innocents' responsory (78:2–3, 12-28), the Common of Martyrs (78:1, C3). Hard readings: 78:9 *propítius esto peccátis nostris* (the glossary's open question), 78:1 *in pomórum custódiam*, 78:10–10b (the sentence crosses the verse break), 78:11 *pósside* (rule 3), 78:8 *antícipent*.

Hard checks pass. 78:1b 'uma' dropped (+4 → +3), accepted: 'cabana de guardar frutos' is the whole image. Length flags accepted: 78:4a +4 (43:14's shared words, copied), 78:6a +3 (articles and possessives Portuguese needs), 78:9b +3 ('sede clemente com' for 'propítius esto' — the ruling), 78:12b −4 (the named subject carries ipsórum; the Latin's quod-clause is heavy), 78:13a +3 (articles before possessives, rule 5), 78:13b −6 (the settled formula 'De geração em geração'). No rhyme flags.
No majors, 1 minor. Passed the propítius ruling, the fruit-watcher's hut, the future irascéris in finem, and the 10/10b sentence. The minor refused and kept as an option.

audit.note: 22 readings, 8 unknown words (macularam, cabana de guardar frutos, escárnio, afronta, iniquidades, acorrentados, seio, afrontaram). The test of the propitius ruling: *sede clemente com os nossos pecados* heard FIRST as 'forgive our sins', 'be lenient toward (tolerate)' second — no reading of favouring the sins. Acted on: 78:1 storage shed (new noun), 78:3 'no one who was buried' (object supplied), 78:10b entre as preposition (chegue). Kept: 78:10 hanging line (the Latin's sentence crosses the break; 'conhecida' points forward), santos, zelo, tomai posse, seio, glossary words.

audit.note: v2: 78:1 cabana de vigia do pomar; 78:3 quem os sepultasse; 78:5 como fogo se acenderá; 78:8 venham ao nosso encontro; 78:10b chegue à vossa presença; 78:12 sete vezes first. New decisions adjuva, introeat. Hard checks pass; 78:8a now +3, 78:1b +3, accepted. Latinist gate owed on 78:1, 78:8, 78:10b.
Gate on v2: no majors, 3 minor, all held as options. 'The translation is faithful throughout.'

outcomes.remark: cabana / pomar make the image explicit; como guarda de frutos
outcomes.reason: 'guarda de frutos' is not heard as a place at all; ὀπωροφυλάκιον is the hut; both v1 readers wanted a named thing.

outcomes.remark: gentes / nationes both nações; entre as gentes
outcomes.reason: one Greek word (D15); 'da gente' is barred in Brazil (the gentes row, 42:1); the Latinist himself says the meaning is unchanged.

outcomes.remark: intróeat 'enter', chegue weakens
outcomes.reason: 'entre' after two prepositional 'entre' was misheard by two v1 readers; a wrong first hearing outweighs a slight weakening (D2).
